description: Wanderguess game rules. Every rule the game enforces lives here, never as a literal in source.

tiers._comment: The tier the 360 viewer was built for. Every other tier is reasoned out from architecture, vegetation and which side of the road the cars drive on; this one can be SOLVED by looking around for a street sign, which turns the panorama from evidence into a puzzle with the answer hidden in it.
tiers.label: Street
tiers.question: Which street?

_difficultyComment: Difficulty is a match setting like scope, and orthogonal to it. Scores are comparable within a match and meaningless across modes - exactly the caveat that already applies to a Europe match versus a world match - so no mode awards different points. Hard is deliberately unfiltered: 'anywhere, significant or not' includes the landmarks, and filtering them out would make hard mode a smaller pool than the game had before difficulty existed.

difficulties.label: Easy
difficulties.blurb: A world-famous landmark is in view, and you start facing it.

difficulties.label: Medium
difficulties.blurb: A major city, with nothing iconic to give it away.

difficulties.label: Hard
difficulties.blurb: Anywhere at all - a city street, a village, an empty road.

_viewerComment: Auto-pan sweeps the view continuously so a player can watch a full 360 without dragging. 6 degrees a second is one revolution a minute - slow enough to read a street sign as it goes past, which is the point now that the street tier asks for one.
_viewerDefaultComment: On by default (owner's call, 2026-08-14): a round should start showing the player around rather than waiting to be asked. The escape hatch is what makes that safe - any click, touch, drag or scroll hands control straight back, and the button then reads Auto-pan again. It is still suppressed for a visitor whose system asks for reduced motion; see respectsReducedMotion.
_reducedMotionComment: prefers-reduced-motion is a visitor telling their own operating system not to animate things at them, which is a different statement from this app's default. Honouring it costs one player a sweep they can start with one button, and ignoring it means a page that moves on its own for someone who asked the whole web not to. Set false to override.

victoryCondition.description: Every player takes one turn per round on a different location. After the configured number of rounds the highest total wins; equal totals are reported as a shared win.

_attributionComment: Licence compliance, not decoration. Two of these are REQUIRED and were missing: GeoNames is CC BY 4.0 and supplies every country, region and city distractor, and OpenStreetMap is ODbL - which requires 'OpenStreetMap contributors' to be credited wherever its data appears - and now supplies every street answer and street distractor, plus the Nominatim verification behind every city and region. Both were in the pipeline long before either was on screen.

attribution.author: Geoff Myers
attribution._sourcesComment: The full credit list, rendered on the setup screen. The game board shows the short form, because a per-round bar has to stay out of the way of the panorama.

sources.what: every street-level panorama, credited to its contributor on each round

sources.name: OpenStreetMap contributors
sources.what: street names and their alternatives, via Nominatim and the Overpass API

sources.name: GeoNames
sources.what: country, region and city names, and the wrong answers offered beside them

sources.name: Wikidata
sources.what: the landmarks easy mode is built around

attribution._softwareComment: Not legally required - these are permissive licences whose notices ship inside the bundle - but a page that lists its data sources and not the software it was built on is telling half the story.
